artifacts.summary: Implementation summary for the /sapience command: draft assembly, design record, and the single approval-gated write picker.

completion_data.completion_summary: Added the /sapience command (commands/sapience.md) and skill-sapience (direct-execution, no Agent tool) to the sapience extension: a bound-project draft assembled from local and vault state, with every outward write gated behind one AskUserQuestion approval picker over sapience-publish.sh's four write surfaces. Wired manifest.json, EXTENSION.md, README.md, and the top-level extensions README; regenerated the deployed tree and confirmed byte-identical artifacts, zero new check-extension-docs.sh findings, and eager-context budget headroom intact.

memory_candidates.content: verify-touched.sh's bare no-argument form derives touched paths from the whole shared working tree's git status, not just the calling task's own edits. In a concurrent multi-task /orchestrate batch this pulls in every sibling task's own uncommitted/committed changes (observed: ~21 unrelated paths across 5 sibling tasks). When a plan phase's Verification bullet already names an explicit path list ('<all touched paths>'), use that explicit invocation instead of the bare no-arg form -- it is both more scoped and matches the phase's own literal wording.

check-extension-docs.sh's Phase-6-style closing verification criterion naming specific rule letters (A, E, R, T, U, check_readme_vs_manifest) is deliberately narrower than 'zero findings for this extension' -- a FAIL from an unnamed rule (e.g. Rule F, deployed-vs-source script content drift) for a file genuinely outside the task's FILE SCOPE does not block closure. Confirm which rule produced a given FAIL line before treating it as this task's own defect.

test-mcp-merge-target.sh (an isolated scratch-project MCP-merge fixture testing hand-written-entry survival across a force-reload+unload cycle) has now been independently observed failing by three separate tasks on the same machine under heavy concurrent multi-agent load, with zero connection to any of their own edited files, and reproduces identically in a fully standalone re-run. Treat a NEW failure from this specific suite as an environment/load-induced flake worth a quick cross-check against other tasks' issue logs before investigating further, not as a signal about the current task's own changes.

sapience_notes.subject: GET /v1/people response shape
sapience_notes.value: Returns {ok, people: [{id, name, ...}], count, me, me_id} -- confirmed live via sapience-project-bind.sh's existing usage pattern, reused for the /sapience command's collaborator resolution (named --message <Name> and the bare --message picker).

sapience_notes.subject: sapience_post dry-run output shape
sapience_notes.value: Under SAPIENCE_DRY_RUN=1, sapience_post prints 'POST <url-with-redacted-token>' then the JSON body (with .token merged to a redacted placeholder if the body is an object) on stdout, makes no network call, and returns 0. This is the exact mechanism the /sapience approval picker's literal-payload preview relies on: the same construction path produces both the dry-run preview and, with --confirm appended, the confirmed write.

sapience_notes.subject: sapience-vault-read.sh failure-mode ordering constraint
sapience_notes.value: sapience_api_init failing inside sapience-vault-read.sh is a hard exit 1 with NO envelope printed at all -- so a caller that wants to check the repo's project binding (repo.binding) cannot rely on the envelope when no token/host resolves. A binding-gate check must read .sapience/project.json directly, independent of whether the vault read would otherwise succeed.

sapience_notes.subject: EXTENSION.md 60-line ceiling
sapience_notes.value: agent-system/extensions/sapience/EXTENSION.md sat at exactly 60 lines with zero slack before adding its first command surface -- check-extension-docs.sh's Rule U caps this file at 60 lines per extension, and it also feeds the eager .claude/CLAUDE.md assembly gate 20 budgets against. A new command surface in an extension already at this ceiling must be authored as an in-place net-zero-line replacement of existing prose, not an append.

sapience_notes.subject: sapience-publish.sh ko subcommand project-key resolution
sapience_notes.value: The ko subcommand cannot read the project KEY from .sapience/project.json (which structurally only ever carries {project (cid), name, repo}); it resolves the short key at runtime via GET /v1/people/projects, matching the binding's cid against that list's entries, and refuses loudly (no write) if no match is found -- never falling back to the binding's free-text name field.
